title: 「Little did someone know that ...」表示當時完全不知道
titleZh: 「Little did someone know that ...」表示當時完全不知道

formula: Little + did + person + know + that + complete clause

formulas.formula: Little + did + person + know + that + complete clause

example: Little did he know that his small decision would change the entire project.
exampleZh: 他當時完全不知道，他那個小決定會改變整個項目。

examples.en: Little did he know that his small decision would change the entire project.
examples.zh: 他當時完全不知道，他那個小決定會改變整個項目。
examples.highlight: Little did he know that his small decision would change the entire project.

meaning.zh: 這個句型表示某人在當時完全不知道一項重要、意外或後來才發現的事實，常用來製造懸念和轉折。

rules.zh: 在這裏表示「完全不知道」 這裏的 little 並不是指「細小」或「少量」。 Little did he know... 相等於： He had no idea... He did not know at all...
rules.en: Here, little means “had no idea” or “did not know at all”; it does not mean small or a small quantity.

rules.zh: 放在句首後，要使用倒裝 正常語序： He did not know that the door was open. 倒裝語序： Little did he know that the door was open. 正確順序是： Little + did + subject + know 不能寫成： Little he did know... ✗ Little he knew... ✗
rules.en: When Little begins the sentence, use inversion in the order Little + did + subject + know.

rules.zh: 後面必須使用原形 know 正確： Little did she know... 錯誤： Little did she knew... ✗ did 已經表示過去時間，所以 know 不可以再變成 knew。
rules.en: Use the base form know after did, not the past form knew.

rules.zh: 後面必須接完整子句 正確： Little did Tom know that the shop had closed. that 後面的子句包括： ● the shop：主語 ● had closed：動詞 錯誤： Little did Tom know that the closed shop. ✗
rules.en: Follow that with a complete clause containing its own subject and verb.

rules.zh: 這個句型主要用於過去的故事 它通常表示： ● 某人在當時不知道一件事； ● 那件事後來被發現； ● 結果帶有驚訝、轉折或意外。 例如： Little did Mia know that her photo would become famous. Mia 當時不知道這件事，但說故事的人已經知道後來的結果。
rules.en: The structure is mainly used in past narratives when a character did not know a later-discovered, surprising or important fact.

rules.zh: 表示「從當時角度看將會發生」 Little did he know that his decision would change the project. 作出決定時，改變項目仍是未來的事情，因此使用： would + 動詞原形
rules.en: Use would + base verb for an event that was still in the future from the character’s past point of view.

rules.zh: 這個句型帶有較強的故事語氣 普通說法： He had no idea that the letter would change his life. 較有故事感的說法： Little did he know that the letter would change his life. 兩句的基本意思相同，但第二句更能製造懸念和意外感。
rules.en: The structure has a strong narrative tone. It expresses the same core fact as “had no idea” but creates more suspense and surprise.

benefits.zh: 讓故事更有懸念 這個句型告訴讀者，人物當時並不知道一件重要的事。 讀者會想繼續了解事情後來如何發展。 Little did Sara know that someone was waiting for her outside.
benefits.en: It creates suspense by revealing that a character did not know an important fact at the time.

benefits.zh: 清楚表達「當時不知道，後來才知道」 它可以把兩個時間角度放在同一句中： ● 人物在過去並不知道； ● 說故事的人現在知道後來的結果。 這樣能令事件的先後關係更清楚。
benefits.en: It clearly contrasts what the character knew then with what the narrator later knows.

benefits.zh: 強調事情出乎意料 He did not know... 只是普通地說某人不知道。 Little did he know... 則強調後來的結果完全超出他的預期。
benefits.en: It emphasises that the later result was unexpected, more strongly than an ordinary “did not know” sentence.

benefits.zh: 讓句子有不同的開頭 學生經常以人物主語開始句子： He... She... Tom... The students... 以 Little 開始句子，可以增加句式變化，避免每句都使用相同開頭。
benefits.en: It gives sentences a different opening and avoids repeatedly beginning with a person’s name or pronoun.

benefits.zh: 可以代替較長的解釋 較長說法： At that time, she had no idea about what would happen later. 目標句型： Little did she know what would happen later. 第二句更集中，也更有故事感。
benefits.en: It can replace a longer explanation such as “At that time, she had no idea what would happen later.”

benefits.zh: 適合故事、演講和個人經歷 這個句型特別適合： ● 故事寫作； ● 個人經歷； ● 小說或電影簡介； ● 口頭講故事； ● 描述意外結果； ● 引出重要轉折。
benefits.en: It is useful in stories, speeches, personal experiences, film or novel summaries and descriptions of unexpected turning points.
